availability_note: Spot is sold through Boston Dynamics' sales team: the Spot sales page asks buyers to contact the team to find the right implementation for their application.

named_models.name: Reinforcement-learning locomotion controller
named_models.role_note: Boston Dynamics says it has integrated reinforcement learning into Spot's locomotion control system, which has historically used model predictive control.

hardware.sensors: Terrain sensing with a 360° horizontal field of view and a 4 m range, and built-in stereo cameras. The optional arm's gripper adds time-of-flight, IMU, and 4K RGB sensors.
hardware.actuation: A maximum speed of 1.6 m/s, a 300 mm maximum step height, and a 14 kg payload limit. The optional arm has six degrees of freedom plus a gripper, reaches 984 mm at full extension, and lifts up to 11 kg.
hardware.power: A 564 Wh battery with an average run time of 90 minutes and a 60-minute recharge. Missions can be launched from the Spot Dock.

developer_access: The Spot SDK's Python client library can control Spot and read its sensor and health information. Its network compute bridge runs a model you have trained on a compute payload or a networked server, and your script commands the robot with the results. The Joint Control API, a beta that needs a special-permissions licence, streams low-level joint commands. Boston Dynamics' own demo drove Spot with Google's Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5 through the SDK.
terms_note: The Spot SDK ships under Boston Dynamics' own Software Development Kit License. The website's Terms of Use say Boston Dynamics' obligations for its products are governed solely by the agreements under which they are provided, and those purchase agreements are not published. The specification sheet mentions a one-year limited warranty.
not_verified: The reinforcement-learning controller and the SDK's model interfaces are Boston Dynamics' own claims; the Atlas has not verified them. Every source is a Boston Dynamics web page or repository file that Boston Dynamics can change at any time.
